featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pritam Pure Veg is one of those places that carries a lot of nostalgia for people who have grown up around Goregaon East. This is a very old and well-known restaurant, serving customers for many years, and for me personally, it has been a part of my childhood. Over the years, I have visited this place countless times — before school, after college, and even now for a quick bite — so this review comes from long-term familiarity rather than a one-time visit.

The biggest strength of Pritam has always been its convenient location near Goregaon East station. It’s the kind of place you naturally stop at when you’re in a hurry, waiting for a train, or looking for a quick breakfast or snack. Even today, it serves that purpose well. Items like snacks, quick meals, and breakfast options are still decent and filling, making it a reliable choice for people on the go.

That said, the taste of the food has definitely changed over time. Compared to how it was years ago, the flavours are not as rich or consistent as they used to be. Long-time customers will notice that the quality has slightly degraded with time. However, it’s still fairly decent, especially when you consider the price point and the fast-paced crowd they cater to. While it may not give you that “wow” feeling anymore, it still does the job when you want something quick and familiar.

The restaurant has a very old-school charm. It’s not fancy, and it doesn’t try to be. The setup is simple and functional, reflecting its age and legacy. Cleanliness is maintained reasonably well considering the heavy footfall, though there is definitely room for modernization and improvement in ambience.

Service is usually quick, which is important given the station crowd. The staff is used to handling rush hours and manages orders efficiently, even if the hospitality feels basic rather than warm or personalized.

Overall, Pritam Pure Veg continues to hold its place as a dependable, no-frills vegetarian restaurant near Goregaon East station. While the food quality may not match the standards of its earlier years, it still remains a decent option for breakfast, snacks, or a quick meal when you’re short on time.

For me, this place is more about memories than perfection. Despite the gradual decline in taste, it still deserves appreciation for its longevity, consistency, and convenience. A solid 4-star experience for nostalgia, accessibility, and reliability — with hope that they focus on improving food quality in the future.

Having always wanted to visit Lucky Restaurant, the legendary Bandra West institution famous for a Biryani so iconic it is famously loved by actor Salman Khan’s family, I was thrilled to try their brand-new branch in Goregaon East.
We started with the Chicken Manchow Soup, which was served remarkably hot and tasted fantastic with a rich, delicious, masala-based flavor, though a few unblended chunks occasionally disrupted the texture. featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our recent visit to Lucky Biryani turned out to be a delicious journey through rich Mughlai flavours, ending with some comforting desserts that rounded off the meal perfectly.

We ordered the Murg Musallam, and it was easily the highlight of our meal. A whole chicken, richly marinated and cooked in a thick, aromatic gravy made with a blend of spices, nuts, and cream – the dish was indulgent, flavorful, and felt true to its royal roots. The chicken was tender, infused with spices, and the gravy was luscious without being overly heavy. The quantity was more than sufficient for two to three people and extremely filling, making it great value for money.

To go along with it, we had Butter Garlic Naan – soft, perfectly cooked with a generous brush of butter and a strong hit of garlic that paired beautifully with the Musallam.

For dessert, we tried the Arabian Pudding, a milk-based sweet that was delicate and smooth, with hints of cardamom and saffron. It was light and refreshing after the rich main course.

We also had the Caramel Custard, which was classic and well-done – creamy, just the right amount of sweetness, and topped with a golden layer of caramel that melted on the tongue.

Overall, Lucky Biryani delivered a satisfying meal – flavour-packed, generously portioned, and rounded off with nostalgic desserts. A great spot if you’re in the mood for classic Mughlai fare done right.
